In `_modulo_reset_times`, it takes the absolute value of the evaluated period and returns an empty reset list when the period is zero or non-finite:
```python
period = np.abs(...)
...
if not np.isfinite(period) or period == 0:
    return np.empty(0)
```
Consequently, negative periods are silently converted to positive periods, while zero and NaN periods silently disable discontinuity handling instead of raising `pybamm.SolverError`. An infinite positive period can legitimately have no resets, but that does not justify silently accepting the other invalid values.

There is also a sensitivity-restart bypass in `_restart_from_solutions`: it only extracts and validates requested sensitivities when `model.y0S_list is not None`. If sensitivities are requested but that list is absent, it continues without raising an error.

The explicit `SolverError` checks for time-dependent periods and missing sensitivity names are good, but they do not eliminate these silent-continuation paths.
